sourceOccurrences.label: The integer-moment Fourier bridge
sourceOccurrences.locator: Section 4.1.1–4.1.2, Lemma 4.1 and (4.4)–(4.13), printed pp.567–569 / PDF indices37–39
sourceOccurrences.relationship: Written integer-order argument with denominator regularization and explicit Fejer justification of convolution sums
sourceOccurrences.note: Mixed derivatives and the spatial bound are proved from absolute moments. Even coordinate weights give the convolution bounds. Fractional orders and the two-mark diagram lemma remain separate.

proofUses.reason: Moment bounds and evenness control differentiated numerator and denominator; induction on the quotient identity gives the uniform regularized derivative estimate.
Integration by parts is first performed with a positive denominator regularization; L1 convergence passes to the critical inverse integral.
Holder bounds and positive Fejer multipliers identify finite-support convolutions; monotone convergence gives the nonnegative critical sums.
The completed critical Fourier bootstrap supplies the gap and second moments, giving the first spatial bound and weighted bubble/triangle sums without assuming spatial decay.
